questions.question: When checking the exhaust system, which of these is NOT a problem?

options.text: Exhaust system parts that are not rubbing against fuel system parts

questions.correctAnswerText: Exhaust system parts that are not rubbing against fuel system parts
questions.explanation: When checking the exhaust system, watch for: loose, broken, or missing pipes, mufflers, or tailpipes; loose or broken mounting brackets, clamps, bolts, or nuts; exhaust parts rubbing against fuel system parts, tires, or other vehicle parts; and leaking exhaust parts.

questions.question: A distracted driver may be:
questions.explanation: You can tell a driver is distracted if they drift between lanes, drive at changing speeds, use a cell phone or look at maps or food, or talk to passengers.

questions.question: A tired driver:

options.text: Should take over-the-counter pills to stay awake.
May react and decide too slowly.
Is usually more careful than other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: May react and decide too slowly.
questions.explanation: When you are tired, you cannot see or react to dangers as quickly. You will have trouble making quick, safe decisions.

questions.question: Keeping emergency equipment on a bus is:

options.text: A good idea if there is extra space.
A good idea if there are more than 15 passengers.

questions.explanation: All commercial vehicles must have emergency equipment. This includes a fire extinguisher, reflectors, and spare fuses if needed.

questions.question: While driving, you should:

options.text: Plan how to handle any dangerous situation.
Focus only on your own driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Plan how to handle any dangerous situation.
questions.explanation: Always watch the road ahead for dangers. Make a plan for any hazard you see coming.

questions.question: If you double your speed from 20 mph to 40 mph, what happens to your braking distance?
questions.explanation: Higher speed increases how far your vehicle will go before stopping. Doubling your speed from 20 to 40 mph makes your braking distance four times longer.

questions.question: The posted design speed for a curve is:

options.text: Safe for all vehicles, including buses.

questions.explanation: Even in good weather, a bus driven at the posted speed could roll over or slide off the road. You should slow down before turning a bus around a curve.

questions.question: A bus driver's seat must have:

options.text: A pocket on the left side.
A pocket on the right side.

questions.explanation: The driver's seat on a bus must have a seat belt that the driver should always wear.

questions.question: When passengers leave the bus, when should you remind them to take their bags?
questions.explanation: Before the bus comes to a complete stop, remind passengers to take their carry-on bags with them.

questions.question: The front of an enclosed trailer should:
questions.explanation: When inspecting an enclosed trailer, check the front for damage like cracks, bulges, or holes.

questions.question: When approaching a curve during the on-road driving test, which of the following should you NOT do?

options.text: Reduce your speed before entering the curve.
Keep your vehicle in its lane.
Use the brakes steadily throughout the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the brakes steadily throughout the curve.
questions.explanation: When approaching a curve, check traffic in all directions. Slow down before you enter the curve so you do not need to brake or shift gears while turning. Stay in your lane and keep checking traffic.

questions.question: What is the standee line?

options.text: A line on the bus floor that passengers cannot cross.
A single-file line of standing passengers.
A mark that shows the maximum number of people allowed on a bus.
A line that shows how tall passengers on a bus may be.

questions.correctAnswerText: A line on the bus floor that passengers cannot cross.
questions.explanation: While a bus is moving, passengers cannot stand in front of the standee line. This line is marked on the bus floor (usually two inches wide) to show where standing passengers must stay. It is located at the rear of the driver's seat.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT acceptable emergency equipment?
questions.explanation: Required emergency equipment includes: spare electrical fuses, three red reflective triangles, six fuses, or three liquid burning flares, and a working fire extinguisher.

questions.question: If you see an aggressive driver who has crashed on the road ahead, what should you do?

options.text: Block in the driver with your vehicle.
Stop safely and tell police about the aggressive driving you saw.
Pull over and yell at the driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop safely and tell police about the aggressive driving you saw.
questions.explanation: If you see a crash involving an aggressive driver, stop at a safe distance from the crash. Wait for police to arrive and report the aggressive behavior you witnessed.

questions.question: Which statement about winter driving is NOT true?

options.text: Front tires should have a tread depth of at least 4/32 of an inch.
Rear tires should have a tread depth of at least 2/32 of an inch.
Use a gauge to check that each tire has safe tread depth.

questions.explanation: In winter, your tires must have good tread. Front tires need at least 4/32 of an inch of tread. Rear tires need at least 2/32 of an inch. Check tread depth with a gauge. Do NOT deflate your tires.

questions.question: If you park on the side of the road, what should you do?

options.text: Let your taillights alert other drivers.
Turn on your emergency flashers to warn other drivers.
Keep your lights off so you do not distract other drivers.
Keep your door open to warn other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your emergency flashers to warn other drivers.
questions.explanation: Always turn on your emergency flashers when you stop on the side of the road. This is especially important at night. Taillights alone are not enough because other drivers may think your vehicle is moving normally.

questions.question: Which of the following is required emergency equipment?

options.text: A supply of spare electrical fuses.

questions.correctAnswerText: A supply of spare electrical fuses.
questions.explanation: Required emergency equipment includes: a fire extinguisher, spare electrical fuses (unless your vehicle has circuit breakers), and warning devices for parked vehicles (such as reflective triangles).

questions.question: When are drivers usually the least alert?
questions.explanation: Drivers are least alert when driving at night, especially after midnight.

questions.question: What is the maximum safe amount of play on a 20-inch steering wheel?
questions.explanation: A steering wheel with more than 10 degrees of play may be defective. On a 20-inch wheel, 10 degrees equals about two inches of movement at the rim.

questions.question: During driving exercises other than straight line backing, how many times can you exit your vehicle to check its position?
questions.explanation: You may exit your vehicle to check its position during any basic control skills test. During straight line backing, you may do this only once. During other exercises, you may do this up to two times.
